source.title: Flat Loss, Evolving Features: Grokking in Modular Addition

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking-like delayed generalization and feature progress on modular addition using supported-Polar hidden updates, normalized head updates, and measures including raw cross-entropy, held-out accuracy, and Fourier fraction.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own modular-addition results and theorem guarantees, so it tests the claim. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as results. Hyperparameter-selection statistics, plotted values without textually stated numbers, and auxiliary experiments not needed to characterize the tested versions are omitted.
record.test_reason: Uses a different optimizer recipe (supported-Polar hidden steps, normalized head steps, weight decay) on modular addition. From iid initializations it reports held-out accuracy rising long after training fit, crossing times across training fractions, and progress measures (Fourier fraction, train-only refit) against the network's own rise. These bear on V1 and V2. The theorems use engineered initializations built to produce the behaviour, so they are existence results rather than tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that relatively flat positive training CE can coexist with evolving features and delayed generalization, proven for 1HL networks from constructed regions and shown empirically from iid init. Qualifications the paraphrase should add: at p=47/61 the deeper nets meet only a post-hoc criterion (primary endpoint 9/160); the transformer result depends on a slowly decaying output gain; two blocks lose the training fit later.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition but replaces the original training recipe with supported-Polar hidden updates, normalized head updates, and weight decay; measures raw CE, held-out accuracy, Fourier fraction, and train-only refits. Experiments include fresh iid starts, constructed theoretical starts, deeper ReLU networks, and transformers.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with depth, prime, training fraction, last-layer rate, feature update, output-gain decay, and held-out mirror-pair definition. On the transformer, fixed gain makes CE fall during the held-out rise and no tested fixed-gain run passes; two blocks later lose training fit. Deeper-network outcomes depend on tuning and window criterion.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out recovery coexists with flat or rising positive training CE. Whether CE rises depends on output-gain decay and training fraction; with fixed gain, CE falls during the rise but generalization still occurs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During grokking the training cross-entropy can stay flat or rise at a positive level while held-out accuracy recovers; a loss plateau is not a learning plateau.

fits_no_version.finding: Two finite-window theorems from constructed initializations guarantee perfect training accuracy, near-flat CE, Fourier-fraction gain and delayed held-out recovery (refit-first in Theorem 4.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: There exist initializations of 1HL ReLU networks under Polar/normalized updates where delayed generalization and feature progress provably occur within a CE plateau.

record.problems: The main 1HL configuration and window were selected using held-out accuracy on development runs, although the reported headline evaluation uses fresh locked runs. Theoretical guarantees rely on constructed, training-data-dependent initialization regions; entry from iid initialization is not proved. Deeper-network settings involve tuning, some cross-fraction criteria do not require training fit, and the authors report strict first-fit failures. Runs across depths and settings reuse seeds and are dependent. Observations in deeper networks are logged at intervals, and the paper notes numerical rank-cutoff sensitivity.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted extensive auxiliary per-prime and fixed-recipe cohorts, most depth-4 training-fraction rows, bias-update variants, theorem-inspired iid runs, and exploratory transformer settings. The paper states that some fixed-recipe and setting changes fail to recover or fail criteria; the primary rows retain the central behavior and the clearest limiting cases. Relevant locations include Appendices B.3–B.6, C.2–C.6, and D.3–D.5.

untested.parts: Original optimizer recipe (AdamW/standard training). Delay-versus-fraction is measured as absolute 90% crossing time, with the last-layer rate retuned per fraction, in deeper nets at p=47/61 only.
No identification of specific memorizing components or a causal circuit analysis; AH and refits are diagnostics.
No non-algorithmic data, no initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich sweep.
Weight decay is used but no circuit-efficiency, critical-dataset-size or ungrokking test.
No systematic comparison of algorithms across runs; only an incidental frequency-count contrast between 1HL and transformer (see missing).
No test of adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax float limits as the cause of the delay (all runs float64, non-adaptive steps).

missing.what: Refit crosses 50% held-out before the network in every depth-3/4 setting at p=47/61, by median 1.2k–9.5k updates (Lead column).
Over the 1HL window, centered energy falls to 0.204–0.209 of its start while addition-subspace energy grows only 1.22–1.31×, so the AH gain is mostly suppression of non-addition energy.
Representation-first flags pass in 0/120 deep p=31 runs. Authors: no uniform refit-before-head chronology or causal role for Fourier growth is established.
A train-only logistic probe on the transformer tracks the network rather than leading it (median leads 0.02k–0.19k).

1HL hidden features carry held-out signal at every frequency, while the transformer head input carries only 6–13 frequencies; the authors compare this with all-frequency versus five-frequency solutions in prior work.
missing.locator: Appendix D.5 'Why the same refit leads'

missing.what: 1HL recipes at 50% training fraction did not recover within 40k updates.

record.verdict_notes: Recipes and windows were selected using held-out accuracy on development runs, and evaluation runs reuse seeds across depths, so cohorts are dependent. The delay-versus-fraction evidence is confounded by a per-fraction last-layer rate. Theorem rows were relinked to none because the behaviour is engineered by construction. The fixed-gain transformer rows were mis-stated as V1 absent; those runs still generalize fully. R31 was wrongly listed under a V2 label in the reader's guesses.

versions.untested_parts: No test of the original optimizer recipe; most results remain on modular addition. The training-fraction timing comparison is reported for selected deeper-network settings and does not establish the general rule for all architectures or tasks.
Does not identify or track specific memorizing components being removed. Fourier fraction and train-only readouts are diagnostics, not a causal identification of a single circuit.
No images, text, molecules, or other non-algorithmic datasets; no lazy-to-rich transition test or controlled initialization-scale sweep.
No realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning data or training stage.
Weight decay is used, but the study does not test whether it selects a more efficient circuit, predict a critical dataset size, or demonstrate ungrokking below one.
No systematic identification or comparison of the algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.

No targeted test of adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax floating-point limits as the cause of grokking. Float64 and optimizer comparisons do not establish that the proposed artifacts are controlled.
